messages.content: You coach a learner of Spanish (their own language is English) who is rewriting part of a real post before publishing it. Two people talk to them: a reader from the community, who speaks Spanish and reacts like a real person in the thread, and a tutor, who speaks Spanish and addresses the learner informally, as a friendly tutor would. The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in Spanish.

Where it will be posted: Correo electrónico. Readers: La Sra. Morales, de la escuela de idiomas a la que quiere aplicar.
What the writer told the tutor about their post while revising (facts about their work and their meaning; take them as true):
- About "Necesito una respuesta antes de fin de mes porque tengo qu…": Presentar el plazo como una necesidad puede sonar a presión hacia una persona que no te conoce; cómo pedir la respuesta depende de lo que quieras transmitir.
The post so far:
<<<
Estimada Sra. Morales:

Mi nombre es Daniel y yo soy de Manchester, en Inglaterra. Le escribo porque quiero solicitar plaza en el curso de septiembre. Vengo a mejorar mi español porque mi novia es de Granada. El año pasado conocí a su familia, pero no entendí casi nada, y tengo muchas ganas de aprender para poder hablar con ellos.

¿Es posible que usted me envíe información sobre los precios? También tengo algunas preguntas. Primero, prefiero una habitación con familia / un piso compartido, no sé cual es mejor para aprender. ¿Es el piso cerca de la escuela? Necesito una habitación tranquila para estudiar. Segundo, ¿puedo traer mi bicicleta? Me gusta montar en bici y quiero explorar las montañas. Tercero, no soy exigente, pero no como carne y espero que la familia pueda preparar algo para mí. Mi novia viene conmigo el primer fin de semana.

¿Me puedes decir cuándo empiezan los cursos? Necesito una respuesta antes de fin de mes porque tengo que comprar el vuelo. Estoy seguro de que lo voy a pasar muy bien en su escuela. Mirando adelante a oír de usted.

Saludos,
Daniel Clarke
>>>
The spot: "Necesito una respuesta antes de fin de mes porque tengo que comprar el vuelo." in Necesito una respuesta antes de fin de mes porque tengo que comprar el vuelo.
What is wrong there: Presentar el plazo como una necesidad puede sonar a presión hacia una persona que no te conoce; cómo pedir la respuesta depende de lo que quieras transmitir.
What the writer means (confirmed by them): Quiero decir que presentar el plazo como una necesidad puede sonar a presión a alguien que no te conoce, así que la forma de pedir la respuesta depende de lo que quieras transmitir.
The learner will now write this part themselves in Spanish. Prepare everything the session needs, in this order:
- reader: what the reader says on reaching this spot as it stands: one short line in Spanish (at most 15 words), in character (puzzled, curious, teasing; never a teacher). The reader cannot read English: an untranslated passage is simply a gap to them, so react to what is missing and never mention the other language.
- replaces: exactly "Necesito una respuesta antes de fin de mes porque tengo que comprar el vuelo.", copied character for character (the text around it is someone else's business). ref must fit in its place.
- keep: every point, detail, question, hedge and feeling in replaces, as short English notes, in order. The reference must carry each one unless the writer's meaning above drops it.
- ref: the reference version: what a fluent member of this community would write here to say exactly what the writer means, in the writer's voice and register. Keep everything the writer already says that still serves this meaning (their evidence, their reasoning, their own words) and add only what is missing. Never invent facts the writer has not given, here or in what they told you: no scene, event, line or detail from a work, no names, numbers, dates, quotes or personal circumstances. Where the meaning needs one (the evidence, which scene, what happened to them), write a short placeholder in its place, in Spanish, between ⟨ and ⟩ (for example ⟨the scene you mean⟩), and the writer will fill it in. Where the problem is how the sentence is built (order, emphasis, angle, nominalisation), rebuild it the way this community would say it; do not stop at the smallest fix. Keep the strength the writer confirmed: where the problem is how something lands on its reader (too pushy, too blunt) and the writer means a firm need, a request or a demand, say it the way this place says such things politely and keep it firm; never turn it into something optional or a passing wish. Where the writer reached for an image or a joke, use this community's own equivalent if it has one rather than flattening it into plain words. Where the writer built a figure on purpose (a parallel or echo, a deliberate repetition, wordplay), ref keeps the figure and only puts natural words into it; the why note for such a word says the figure works and why the word changes. ref never says again what the post already says right before or after the replaced text (a reason or detail the next sentence gives stays there). ref replaces exactly the replaces text and carries every keep note and every name, title or label in it (a dish's name before its description, a person's name); it is the final text for that span: anything else wrong or unnatural inside it is fixed too, even where it is the writer's own wording. The writer's voice stays: casual spelling and capitalisation (all lowercase, capitals for emphasis, keysmashes, stretched letters, a missing apostrophe in a contraction), slang, emoji and the community's own shorthand, wherever fluent members of this community write that way too; so does a greeting or a word from another language used as flavour that readers will get. Names (characters, people, usernames, places, the community's terms) are the writer's: leave how they spell and capitalise them and which name they use, unless a reader could not tell who is meant. None of these is a problem in either pass. But wording carried over from English (a calque, a collocation, structure or set phrase a fluent writer would not produce) is not voice: it is a problem however casual the post. ref keeps that voice. Put [square brackets] around two to four single words that carry the key choices.
- alts: one or two other natural ways to say it, without brackets.
- pieces: three to eight hint pieces: the content words and short collocations (one to three words) that carry the meaning, including the writer's own words worth reusing. Each piece is Spanish words only: no grammar notes, glosses, symbols or instructions. A piece names a word, never how to use it ("worth", not "worth + -ing" or "worth coming"). Not consecutive chunks of ref, no function-word glue, no full clauses: the learner must still build the sentence. "x / y" offers a fork.
- construct: the one reusable pattern this spot teaches, as a learner would jot it in a notebook: at most eight words, a Spanish frame with one placeholder ("X left him + adjective", "What really got me was …"), optionally a short Spanish gloss. Not a grammar formula.
- why: one entry per choice in ref that the learner might not make themselves. label: the Spanish words; note, in Spanish: why this choice here, contrasted with what the learner wrote or would likely write, with a nuance or a tiny example when it helps. Concrete and specific, never "more natural" or "more appropriate" alone.
- checks: the mistakes this learner is likely to make on a first try, most important first: missing a part of the meaning, a structure carried over from English, the specific error already in their draft, a wrong word for this sense. For each: problem (what the grader should look for, in English); reader (optional: how the reader reacts when it happens, one Spanish line in character, only when the meaning really suffers); hint (Spanish: a nudge that points at the gap without giving the words); tell (Spanish: says the fix plainly, with the words).
- success: the reader's reaction once the learner gets it right: in Spanish, in character, at most 12 words, a reaction to what is now said (not a summary of it).
- prompt: the tutor's instruction in Spanish to start writing: one short sentence that fits the size of the spot (a clause, a sentence, a passage). The writer has just confirmed what they mean, so do not restate it; never mention punctuation, span boundaries or what comes after; never contain any word or structure from ref.
Reply with JSON only: {"reader":"","replaces":"","keep":[],"ref":"","alts":[],"pieces":[],"construct":"","why":[{"label":"","note":""}],"checks":[{"problem":"","reader":null,"hint":"","tell":""}],"success":"","prompt":""}

An earlier answer was not usable: ref still has "una respuesta antes", left as the writer wrote it: write it in Spanish, as the writer means it. Mind that this time.

Todavía no nos conocemos, ¿no?","replaces":"Necesito una respuesta antes de fin de mes porque tengo que comprar el vuelo.","keep":["Necesito una respuesta: a firm need, not an optional wish, so the request must stay firm","antes de fin de mes: the deadline is the end of this month","porque tengo que comprar el vuelo: the reason, that he has to buy the flight","Tone: it must sound polite and not pushy, because the reader does not know him yet"],"ref":"Le [ruego] que me [responda] antes de fin de mes, porque tengo que comprar el vuelo.","alts":["Le agradecería que me respondiera antes de fin de mes, ya que tengo que comprar el vuelo.","Le pido por favor que me conteste antes de fin de mes, porque tengo que comprar el vuelo."],"pieces":["rogar","contestar","plazo","vuelo","mes","urgencia"],"construct":"Le ruego que + verbo en subjuntivo (pedir con firmeza y educación)","why":[{"label":"ruego","note":"«Le ruego» es una petición formal que sigue siendo firme. En cambio, «necesito» en este contexto suena a presión a alguien que no te conoce. Con «ruego» mantienes la urgencia sin exigir."},{"label":"responda","note":"Después de «ruego que» va el subjuntivo: «responda», no «responde». Además, el verbo «responder» suena más natural aquí que «una respuesta antes», que se calca del inglés."},{"label":"antes de fin de mes","note":"Dentro de la petición, el plazo funciona como límite que se pide, no como una obligación tuya. Así el plazo queda claro sin sonar a exigencia."}],"checks":[{"problem":"The request is written as a bare need ('I need…') that reads as pressure on a stranger; the grader should look for a firm but polite way of asking.","reader":"¿Y esa prisa? Todavía no nos conocemos, ¿no?","hint":"Piensa en cómo pedir algo firme a alguien que no te conoce, con una fórmula de cortesía.","tell":"Usa «Le ruego que me responda…» para pedir con firmeza y educación."},{"problem":"After the request phrase the verb is in the indicative (for example 'responde') instead of the subjunctive.","reader":null,"hint":"Fíjate en el modo del verbo que va después de «ruego que».","tell":"Después de «ruego que» va el subjuntivo: «me responda»."},{"problem":"Carried-over English structure: 'una respuesta antes de…' built as a noun phrase instead of a verb.","reader":null,"hint":"Aquí un verbo suena más natural que un sustantivo con «antes».","tell":"Usa el verbo «responder» en lugar de «una respuesta antes»."},{"problem":"The deadline or the reason for it (the flight purchase) is lost in the rewrite.","reader":null,"hint":"Recuerda qué plazo pides y por qué lo necesitas.","tell":"Mantén «antes de fin de mes» y la razón de tener que comprar el vuelo."}],"success":"Ah, así sí da gusto contestar con calma.","prompt":"Escribe cómo pedirle a la Sra. Morales una respuesta, con firmeza pero con educación."}
